title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Order of Multiplication
text:
Order of Multiplication

Key terms: multiplication, order

The order of multiplication does not matter. For example, a × b × c = c × d × a. This can be seen from the area of a rectangle remaining the same even if the length and breadth are interchanged.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Converting Division to Multiplication
text:
Converting Division to Multiplication

Key terms: division, multiplication, reciprocal

Division can be converted to multiplication by finding the reciprocal of the divisor. For example, a ÷ b = a × 1/b. This can be used to divide fractions.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Dividing Fractions
text:
Dividing Fractions

Key terms: division, fractions, reciprocal

To divide fractions, find the reciprocal of the divisor and multiply it by the dividend. For example, a ÷ b = a × b's reciprocal. This can be used to solve division problems involving fractions.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Brahmagupta's Formula for Division
text:
Brahmagupta's Formula for Division

Key terms: Brahmagupta, formula, division

Brahmagupta's formula for division of fractions is a ÷ b = a × b's reciprocal. This formula can be used to solve division problems involving fractions.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Fraction of a Whole
text:
Fraction of a Whole

Key terms: fraction, whole, part

A fraction of a whole represents a part of a whole. It is written as a number of equal parts out of a total number of parts. For example, 1/2 represents one part out of two equal parts.

Key terms: multiplication, fractions, numerator, denominator

To multiply two fractions, we multiply the numerators and denominators separately. For example, 1/2 × 3/4 = (1 × 3) / (2 × 4) = 3/8.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Division of Fractions
text:
Division of Fractions

Key terms: division, fractions, invert, multiply

To divide one fraction by another, we invert the second fraction and multiply. For example, 1/2 ÷ 3/4 = 1/2 × 4/3 = 4/6 = 2/3.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Reciprocal of a Fraction
text:
Reciprocal of a Fraction

Key terms: reciprocal, fraction, numerator, denominator

The reciprocal of a fraction is obtained by swapping the numerator and denominator. For example, the reciprocal of 1/2 is 2/1.

Key terms: Brahmagupta, formula, multiplication, fractions

Brahmagupta's formula states that to multiply two fractions, we multiply the numerators and denominators separately. For example, a/b × c/d = (a × c) / (b × d).

Brahmagupta's formula states that to divide one fraction by another, we invert the second fraction and multiply. For example, a/b ÷ c/d = (a × d) / (b × c).
